### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **87** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d0e4cc8adffda0be957b0455c85f2d2843297dc` — the merge of head `0af89166469cf611a5bfb1cd9cb3c370f44f1b96` into base `f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d0e4cc8adffda0be957b0455c85f2d2843297dc && git checkout 7d0e4cc8adffda0be957b0455c85f2d2843297dc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6 0af89166469cf611a5bfb1cd9cb3c370f44f1b96 && git checkout -B drift-repro f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6 && git merge --no-ff 0af89166469cf611a5bfb1cd9cb3c370f44f1b96

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f727061b88258b946402bbb29afee6e6410081d6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `aa1df8a4a2eb9d9506d34eab51ec33350dfbc085`
Local-runs: none

PR #35450 · card #34681 · face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`, no file under `packages/spec/src`, no governed path). The head is a merge of `main` 6f36818f into 9bb4ae92; the net diff against `main` is the PR's nine files (+464 / −36), and the merge changed none of the PR's own hunks.

Gate verdicts on this head, read from its check-runs at 11:50Z: 24 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 11 still in progress (`Test Core` 1/10 to 10/10 and `Type Check · workspace`). The gates have not all answered yet. The verdict below does not wait on them: it rests on M1.

Findings: one must-fix (M1), three should-fix (S1, S2, S3), three nits.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff implies one accept-set change, at seven doors, in one cell: a bundled type's name that no package ships, held as active rows at one member by a base package and by a package that declares it, with no package-less row beside them.

| Door naming no package | `main` | This head | Judgment |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| save, publish mode (`protocol-save.ts:854-861`) | 409 naming both | writes the base's row; a read-only base answers 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` | right |
| save, draft mode (`protocol-save.ts:900-908`) | 409 naming both | writes the base's draft | right in the pinned cell, wrong at S1 |
| per-item publish (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts:843-848`) | 409 naming both | promotes the base's draft into the base's row | right (nit N1) |
| delete and draft discard (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts:726-749`) | 409 naming both | removes the base's row or draft; the receipt names the dependent's row | right |
| history, diff, rollback (`protocol-history-slots.ts:177-181`) | 409 naming every holder | the base's slot, as the request naming the base resolves it | right |

Why the guard is right. `packagelessRowHeldBaseAddress` (`protocol-save.ts:3245-3268`) answers a base only when the read's own judgment (`rowHeldBaseAddressOf`, unchanged) answers it over the item's active rows, two or more packages are bound at the member, no package-less row sits beside them, and the base is one of those packages. The read serves the base under the same three conditions (`storedRowHoldersRefusal`, `protocol-meta-item-face.ts:477-480`). The read filters declined rows and customization-pair rows before counting and the helper does not, but the judgment itself answers no base when either sits at the member, so the two agree. Every door asks the helper only on the branch that would otherwise refuse naming two or more packages, so no request that succeeded on `main` is refused here: the change is a widening only. The draft doors' `ambiguous` address that reaches the helper is always the active-rows case (`protocol-lock-version-gates.ts:515-518`); two packages' drafts over no active row still refuse.

The read-only base's 409 becoming 422 swaps one refusal for another on a request refused both ways. It narrows nothing; a client that offered a package picker on the 409 now reads the 422 naming the base.

Public surface. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` exports only its index, and neither the facets, `historySlotOf` nor the new helper are in it, so the widened host `Pick` lists and the new export move no published type. The published change is behavioural: the accept set of seven protocol methods.

**M1 (must-fix): the published request contract still says these requests are refused.** `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` states the opposite of this head in four `.describe()` texts, which ship in `@objectstack/spec` and generate `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`:

- `SaveMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`, `:1218-1221` (active save: "is refused 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT when they are bound to two or more") and `:1228-1230` (draft save, the same);
- `PublishMetaItemRequestSchema.packageId`, `:1560-1562`;
- the delete request's `packageId`, `:2434-2435`, and through it the draft discard;
- `HISTORY_PACKAGE_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION`, `:2655-2656` ("Absent, a name two holders hold … is refused 409 naming every holder"), used by the history, diff and rollback requests (`:2720`, `:2993`, `:3056`).

The claim fenced `packages/spec/**`, and neither os-dev-report names these sentences. Landing as it stands ships a release whose protocol reference says "409" where the server writes, deletes and restores. The save description was already amended once for an address rule of this family ("every enabled holder, for an active save"), so the text is kept in step by practice. To close: amend the four descriptions and regenerate (`gen:schema && gen:docs`), either in this PR after a claim amendment lifts the spec fence (the face then becomes schema, and the delta is owed a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review), or on a card of its own that lands ahead of or together with this PR.

**S1 (should-fix): the draft-mode arm skips the named-base rule the bare save owes.** `protocol-save.ts:900-908` rewrites `request.packageId` to the base and clears `draftAddress`. The inherited named-base rule (`:946-954`, #26921) and the late override re-judgment (`:2011-2017`) read a draft save's package from `draftAddress.into`, which is now gone, so in draft mode neither is asked of the base. The publish-mode arm is not affected (`request.packageId` is read there). Reachable cell: the base's rows are bound to an id no installed package has, and an installed dependent declares that id (a declared dependency stays in the closure when it is not installed, `packages/metadata-core/src/package-closure.ts`). There the save naming the base is refused 422 at `:568`, the bare publish-mode save is refused 422 at `:950`, and the bare draft save writes a draft bound to the uninstalled id, which `isWritablePackage` does not catch. On `main` that request was the 409. Derived by reading the code, not measured, and not pinned. To close: have both sites read the re-addressed package in draft mode, and pin the cell.

**S3 (should-fix): contract docblocks the PR left false.** Claim amendment 7005577225 corrected two docblocks on the ground that the PR making a sentence false lands the correction. The same sentence remains in: `protocol.ts:9621-9624` (history), `protocol.ts:11061-11063` (rollback), `protocol.ts:7967-7969` (`packagelessDraftAddress`: "refused by both doors"), `protocol.ts:7876-7879` (`packagelessAddress`), and the module header of `protocol-history-slots.ts:15-19` ("nothing picks one"). Comment-only; same PR.

Nits:
- N1. The per-item publish naming no package states no package to the runtime authoring gate (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts:1245`), where the publish naming the base states the base and is judged against its dependency closure. This is the documented shape of every bare publish on `main`, now reachable in this cell, so "exactly as the same request naming the base" is not exact for that gate. Wording, or a follow-up card.
- N2. Pin coverage: the REST door is driven for `PUT` only (delete, publish, history, diff and rollback are pinned in process); no bare read is asserted after the bare publish before the restart; the read-only base is pinned for the save alone.
- N3. Stale counts in prose: the PR body's two-minute check expects `Tests 5 passed (5)` (the file holds 7), and the pin file's header still says "the five write doors".

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34681-bare-write-doors-follow-base.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body.

- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, accepted value or metadata type moves; the change is which stored row a request naming no package addresses.
- `patch` is right: kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3).
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: requests refused 409 on `main` are accepted, and none accepted on `main` is refused.
- `@objectstack/runtime` gains a test file only and publishes nothing, so it needs no entry.
- M1's spec amendment publishes from `@objectstack/spec` and needs its own changeset wherever it lands.

The changeset's sentence "exactly as the same request naming the base does" is subject to S1 and N1.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and open questions, from os-dev-reports 7005535521 and 7007306366:

- `open_questions[0]` (two docblocks made false): answered A by claim amendment 7005577225 and done in the diff. Incomplete: S3.
- `open_questions[1]` (the diff and the rollback): answered A by the same amendment and done through `historySlotOf`, with the one `Pick` line in `protocol-package-commits.ts`. Pinned, and ablated per the delta report.
- Deviation, no dogfood battery: agreed. `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` owes the full battery only for a `!` title or a `(narrowing)` arm.
- Deviation, a new pin file instead of a describe in the shared harness: agreed, the dispatch fenced that file.
- Deviations on the PR body layout, the mis-spelled test command and the merge commit's trailer: no contract effect.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, class a (a dependent's non-canonical member over a base holding only the canonical one: bare read 404, bare save 200 into the dependent's row, bare read then 409): present on `main`, untouched here, and **not yet filed**. PR comment 7007933229 says a card draft waits. Escalated to area pkg-2: it is a read and write disagreement of the same family and needs its card.
- `out_of_scope_findings`, class b (diff and rollback): closed by this PR.
- `security_findings: none`: this review found no authorization bypass. The lock gate is not narrowed by package, the writable-base gate judges the re-addressed package on the save, the rollback's named-base close judges the resolved slot, and the publish gates judge `promoteInto`. S1 is an integrity gap, not an access one.

**S2 (should-fix): the decision route.** Triage twice reserved this card for a maintainer decision card before code (6940518124, 6945990423), and the card body says a change to the write doors goes to a person. The seat answered with its own note (7000610592) that two standing maintainer rulings already decide it. I read both cited comments, outside this brief's input list, to check that note:

- 6781691009 is an epic-seat ruling, posted on #32354 (not on #31527, and not by the maintainer). It states the general rule ("a write resolves its address exactly as the read at the same address resolves it") and reasons it for the save over an enabled and a disabled holder ("binding the save to E destroys nothing of D's").
- 6942981052 records the maintainer's choice on #34348: the environment's own item answers first, "and reads and writes give the same answer".

The rule sentence covers this cell, and the dispatch rule lets a same-family card reuse a parent ruling with its reasons. The save, draft save, publish and history doors follow directly. The delete, the draft discard and the rollback are destructive doors the ruling's reasons did not weigh: a bare delete that was refused now removes the base's row, after which the bare read serves the dependent's row (A3, measured and pinned). I judge the direction sound, since `packagelessAddress` already binds the save, the delete and the version token to one resolution. But triage's ask stands unanswered by triage or the maintainer. To close: one line on the card from triage or the maintainer accepting the execution route for the destructive doors, or the decision card triage asked for; and correct the attribution of 6781691009 in the claim.

SQL push-down: no finding. The helper adds one read of the item's active rows (`readItemActiveRows`, one `(type, name)`, a handful of rows) on the would-refuse branch only, and judges them against the in-memory package manifests, which SQL cannot reach. No id list is materialised and no join moves into the application. On that branch the item's rows are read up to three times (the door's address, the helper, the history recursion's `rowSlotsOf`); the path is rare and the cost is small.

Another author: none. The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

Before landing: M1 closed; S1, S2 and S3 closed or ruled as accepted deviations; every check-run on the landing head green; then the delta is read by this reviewer.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34681-bare-write-doors-follow-base`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ` (L2 subagent)

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `914e61af518a1b0c26dd63d197684836a709e7fc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-slots.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-bare-write-doors-follow-base-34681.test.ts, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, .changeset/34681-spec-bare-doors-follow-base.md
Security-touching: no

PR #35450 · card #34681 · face: schema (the five `packageId` description texts in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`). This record reads the delta from `aa1df8a4` (my FAIL, PR comment 7008272548) to this head, three commits, and re-judges the whole diff against `main` at this tier. It closes that record's findings by id.

Gate verdicts on this head: every check-run has concluded, read at 13:50Z. 74 runs: 62 success, 12 skipped, 0 failed, 0 in progress. The skipped ones are opt-in, queue-only or schedule lanes (the dogfood shards, the queue verdicts, the upgrade harness, the packed-tarball smoke, `Lint UI`, `Auto Label`, `Check PR Size`). `Check Changeset`, the five `Type Check` lanes, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build Docs` and `Test Core` 1/10 to 10/10 are success.

Result: M1, S1, S2, S3, N1, N2 and N3 are closed. Three new nits (N4, N5, N6), none touching correctness or the contract.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept-set change is the one judged at `aa1df8a4`, and those judgments stand: at seven doors naming no package, in the row-held-base cell, a request refused 409 on `main` now addresses the base's row, draft or versions. Nothing accepted on `main` is refused. The delta adds three things.

1. **The draft save judges the followed base as named (closes S1).** `protocol-save.ts:904-912` keeps the base in `followedBase`; the inherited named-base rule (`:954`) and the late override re-judgment (`:2018`) read it. In the cell S1 named (the base's rows bound to an id no installed package has, declared by an installed dependent) the bare draft save is now refused 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`, as the save naming the base and the bare publish-mode save are. Right. Against `main` this is one refusal for another (409 there), so it narrows nothing. The round-three report measured the old head answering 200 there, which confirms what S1 derived by reading. Pinned at `meta-bare-write-doors-follow-base-34681.test.ts:229`.

2. **The rollback receipt names the package (rider 1).** `protocol-package-commits.ts:2355-2357` adds ` (package=ID)` to the receipt `message` whenever the restored row is bound to a package, in the delete receipt's spelling (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts:986`). This reaches every package-bound rollback, not only this cell. It is message text only: no status, code or field moves, and no reader in the repo parses the sentence. Right, and the changeset declares it.

3. **The published request texts state the exception (closes M1).** Five sentences in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`:
   - save, active: `:1222-1228`; save, draft: `:1236-1237`;
   - per-item publish: `:1569-1573`;
   - delete, and through it the draft discard: `:2448-2457`;
   - `HISTORY_PACKAGE_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION`: `:2677-2681`, read by the history, diff and rollback requests (`:2745`, `:3018`, `:3081`).

   Each now says the row-held base is addressed as naming it does, and that two packages neither of which declares the other are still refused. Description text only: no shape, key or accepted value moves. Right.

Generated reference in sync: `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` changes exactly six rows (`:786` delete, `:860`, `:2162` and `:2970` the three history-selector uses, `:2648` publish, `:3066` save). Each carries the new sentence word for word and none of the four old sentences remains in the page. No other checked-in artifact in the tree carries the old description text.

Public surface: unchanged from the first record apart from the two items above. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` exports only its index; `followedBase` is a local.

### ② Semver level

Two changesets, each with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in its body, as the PR body carries them.

- `.changeset/34681-spec-bare-doors-follow-base.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `patch`. Right. The spec publishes description text and the page generated from it; kind `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, since no key, accepted value or type moves. The `Clause-②` line is the PR's declaration copied into each changeset body, as the dispatch form asks.
- `.changeset/34681-bare-write-doors-follow-base.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch`, unchanged in level. Its body now states the named-base judgment, the rollback receipt, the second bare delete, and that the bare per-item publish states no package to the authoring gate. That closes N1: the sentence no longer says "exactly as".
- `@objectstack/runtime` still gains a test file only and needs no entry.
- No breaking banner and no ADR-0087 entry is owed: nothing narrows against `main`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Findings of record 7008272548, by id:

- **M1: closed.** See ① item 3 and ④.
- **S1: closed.** See ① item 1.
- **S2: closed.** Card comment 7008542936 records the maintainer's choice of option A on the decision card: the bare delete, draft discard and rollback follow the row-held base, with the stated consequence accepted. It is the seat's record of that choice, in the form this repo records rulings. Claim correction 7008307314 fixes the attribution of 6781691009. The three riders are met in the tree: rider 1 at ① item 2; rider 2 in three pins (`:242` two bare deletes in a row, `:256` the bare draft read serves the draft the bare discard removes, `:270` a read-only base at delete, discard and rollback equals the request naming it); rider 3 at ④.
- **S3: closed** for the five sites it named: `protocol.ts` `packagelessAddress`, `packagelessDraftAddress`, `historyMetaItem` and `rollbackMetaItem` docblocks, and the `protocol-history-slots.ts` header. The file stays at 11705 lines. Residue: N5.
- **N1: closed** (②). **N3: closed**: the PR body and the pin header count eleven tests and seven doors.
- **N2: closed.** A bare read is asserted after the bare publish, and the read-only base is pinned at the destructive doors. The delete stays pinned in process: the dispatcher transport answers 405 to `DELETE` on a metadata item by design (`packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:2119-2147`), so the deviation is accepted.

Round-three dev flags (os-dev-report 7010399497): `open_questions` is empty. Deviations: the REST `DELETE` pin, accepted above; the ablation leg re-run with a surviving marker, no contract effect; the stale tree, see the landing note. The class-a out-of-scope finding (a dependent's non-canonical member over a base holding only the canonical one) is still not filed. It stays escalated to area pkg-2 and is not a finding on this PR.

SQL push-down: no finding. The delta adds no read and no query; the first record's judgment of the helper's one bounded read stands.

Another author: none. The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

New nits:

- **N4.** The spec exception names the cell as "a bundled type's member whose active rows a base package and a package declaring it both hold, with no package-unbound row beside them". It leaves out that no package ships the name in code, which the `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` changeset does say. Where the base ships the name, the server still refuses, so the text errs only toward promising a write the server declines, and "as the read naming no package serves it" bounds it. The delete's consequence sentence also assumes one dependent. Tighten on the next touch of these texts.
- **N5.** Three unexported request-shape docblocks in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-door-requests.ts` still state the refusal with no exception: `:67-69` (publish), `:119-121` (rollback), `:151-152` (delete). S3 did not name them. Comment-only, and the published text is now the spec's.
